_comment: DOM selectors for the ESPN fantasy UI. Kept FLAT on purpose — test_login.js and
check_espn_session.js read these keys directly. draft_clicker.js (WORKER-06) and
waiver_sniper.js (#14) no longer do — both were rewritten to drive ESPN's REST/WebSocket
APIs instead of clicking, because the roster/free-agent DOM carries no per-player identifier
(see below). `search_input`, `draft_button` and `waiver_confirm_button` are left here only as
a documented record of what didn't work; nothing in the codebase reads them anymore.
Recon on 2026-08-11 (src/bots/lineup_recon.js, league 1234567890) found that ESPN's roster
table exposes NO per-player identifier in the DOM: `tr[data-player-id]`, `tr[data-playerid]`
and any attribute matching /player.?id/i all return ZERO matches. Rows carry only `data-idx`,
a positional index. That is why lineup_bot.js and waiver_sniper.js drive ESPN's REST API
instead of clicking (see src/bots/espn_api.js).
`roster_table` was `.roster-table`, which matched nothing; it is now the verified `.Table`.
Live capture on 2026-09-12 (a real FLEX/Bench swap against league 1234567890 team 8, confirmed
and then reverted) drove `move_button` and `here_button` end-to-end and both worked as written:
clicking `move_button` on a player puts the row into move mode, then `here_button` on the target
row's own `.Table__TR` completes the move. There is NO separate save_button click needed for a
single move/swap — clicking `here_button` fires the `transactions/` POST immediately (confirmed
via network capture); `button:has-text("Save")` matched zero elements throughout. This is still
just a documented record for any future DOM-driven UI work — espn_api.js's REST path (verified
against this same capture) remains the only production write path; nothing wires these up.
trade_* keys (#90) drive the trade-builder page (/football/team/trade?teamId=<them>&fromTeamId=<us>).
trade_builder.js REFUSES a real submit until every key in its TRADE_SUBMIT_SELECTOR_KEYS is listed
under `_verified`. trade_headshot_img is a template: `{id}` is replaced with the ESPN player id.
Verified 2026-10-03 (#123) by a scripted no-send recon against league 1234567890, team 8 vs team 1,
with trade_builder's write guard on the whole BrowserContext (0 ESPN writes blocked or allowed):
- Each roster row is a .Table__TR holding a visible span[role=checkbox] (aria-checked tracks state)
that wraps a hidden input[type=checkbox]. Playwright check() on the span works.
- Player rows carry img src .../headshots/nfl/players/full/<espnId>.png. A D/ST row instead shows
a team logo and its name link reads just the team name ("Giants"), not readRoster's "Giants D/ST".
- Continue stays on the same URL and opens a review panel: a "Send Trade Proposal" button, a
"Cancel" button, and a textarea with placeholder "Comments to include on the trade proposal".
Continue itself sent no ESPN write.
- The OneTrust consent dialog in the same page has its own "Submit"/"Cancel" buttons and checkbox
toggles, which is why trade_submit_button is the full "Send Trade Proposal" text.
Seen but deliberately NEVER clicked: trade_submit_button. What ESPN sends when it IS clicked is
still uncaptured (#124); until then a live submit can end as an "outcome unknown" fail-closed.

_verified.source: lineup_recon.js + a live driven swap against league 1234567890 team 8, 2026-08-11 / 2026-09-12; trade_* keys: no-send trade-builder recon, 2026-10-03 (#123)

_unverified.warning: Never matched against a real page. Do not assume these work.

_confirmed_absent.note: No separate Save control exists for a single move — here_button alone commits it.
